description: Hi, I’m Phu, a student who enjoys building web apps and exploring sustainability ideas. I’m forming TerraWeave to build RotationLab, a tool combining NASA data and local farming conditions to compare crop rotation options and explain the trade-offs. I bring web prototyping experience and am looking for teammates in coding, data analysis, agriculture, UI/UX, or storytelling. Beginners are welcome—what matters is curiosity, commitment, and learning together. Join me at the Ho Chi Minh event!
summary:
RotationLab is a web-based prototype that helps farmers, agricultural cooperatives, and technical advisers compare crop rotation options and document their decisions. It brings plot information, water constraints, soil conditions, and seasonal crop sequences into a structured planning workflow.

Instead of presenting one recommendation without explanation, RotationLab lets users examine trade-offs across water feasibility, soil nitrogen balance, pest-cycle interruption, and estimated economic performance. An explanation panel helps users inspect the assumptions and supporting information behind individual criteria. Users can then save a decision record containing their reasoning, accepted trade-offs, and required field verification tasks.

The project aims to make agricultural planning more transparent and easier to review. Its value lies in connecting comparisons with accountable human decisions, rather than treating a calculated score as a guaranteed outcome. The current prototype demonstrates the workflow; its agricultural assumptions and input data require local verification before operational use.
details:
What we developed

RotationLab is a browser-based crop rotation planning prototype designed to make agricultural trade-offs visible and decisions traceable. It supports a workflow in which users select a plot, review available input information, choose candidate rotations, compare alternatives, and document a final decision.

How it works

The planning interface uses plot information such as soil characteristics, recorded salinity, and water constraints alongside candidate seasonal crop sequences.

A multi-criteria comparison matrix presents alternatives across water feasibility, soil nitrogen balance, pest and disease cycle interruption, and estimated economic performance. Users can inspect explanations for individual criteria rather than relying only on a composite score.

When saving a decision, users document their technical rationale, the trade-offs they accept, and the field checks that remain necessary. This separates the software’s comparison from the human decision and its supporting justification.

Intended users and benefits

The intended users include agricultural cooperatives, technical advisers, and people involved in farm planning. RotationLab aims to support clearer discussions about competing priorities and preserve the reasoning behind a chosen plan.

Its intended impact is better-informed, more accountable planning—not a guaranteed increase in yield, income, or resource efficiency. Demonstrating those outcomes would require field validation.

Tools and implementation

The interface code shared during development uses React and TypeScript, with utility-based styling and Lucide icons. GitHub supports source-code collaboration, and GitHub Pages is the project’s previously supplied deployment platform.

The comparison workflow uses rule-based evaluations rather than generative AI to write agricultural recommendations.

Creative approach

RotationLab combines comparison, explanation, and decision documentation in one workflow. Rather than stopping at a ranked list, it encourages users to inspect the basis of a result, acknowledge trade-offs, and identify what still needs verification.

Design considerations and limitations

The project considers readability, consistent presentation, responsive layouts, and Vietnamese–English interface text.

Data provenance and uncertainty are important limitations. A value recorded in a plot profile should not automatically be presented as a verified station observation. Likewise, a prefilled statement should not imply that a technical committee has approved a decision.

The current prototype should therefore be presented as a decision-support demonstration, not as a validated agronomic advisory service.
